name: Kodo Rock
summary: Young tauren shamans are sent to Kodo Rock on Red Cloud Mesa, between Camp Narache and Brambleblade Ravine. The stone rises among Mulgore’s grasses and is easy to miss among the rolling hills.

sections.title: A Waypoint on the Mesa
sections.body: Kodo Rock marks the straight path from Camp Narache to Brambleblade Ravine, where hostile quilboar hold territory. Worn earth circles its base. Its shape recalls the kodo beasts that wander the grasslands, though the stone is smaller than the bluffs around Red Cloud Mesa. For tribesfolk crossing Mulgore’s windswept plains, it is a quiet landmark.

sections.title: Spiritual Significance
sections.body: Among the Shu'halo, natural formations carry spiritual weight. Young tauren shamans beginning their spiritual walk are sent to Kodo Rock for their early rites of passage. At the solitary stone, novices commune with elemental forces and honor the natural world. Then they venture into more perilous reaches of the continent.

faq.answer: Kodo Rock stands on Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore, roughly halfway along the straight path between Camp Narache and Brambleblade Ravine. Bare dirt marks a small clearing at its base.

faq.q: Why is Kodo Rock hard to find?
faq.answer: Kodo Rock blends into the mesa’s rolling hills and grasses, and becomes clear only at close range. Look for the patch of dirt beneath it.

faq.q: Why is Kodo Rock important to tauren shamans?
faq.answer: Tauren shamans visit Kodo Rock during their earliest trials out of Camp Narache. Novices are sent there to attune their spirits to Mulgore’s land and elemental forces.

faq.q: What dangers are near Kodo Rock?
faq.answer: The area around Kodo Rock is generally peaceful. Farther northeast, Brambleblade Ravine is held by aggressive Bristleback quilboar.

angles.text: As a shaman beginning the spiritual path at Camp Narache, you are sent to Kodo Rock to attune with the elemental world.
As a tauren, you know Kodo Rock as a landmark on Red Cloud Mesa, a stone that reflects the Shu'halo’s sacred bond with Mulgore’s beasts.
